metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to patch submissions/contributions to QEMU; does not apply to other AI uses such as researching APIs, static analysis, or debugging where output is not included in contributions.
domains.accountability_wording: the "Signed-off-by" label in a patch submission is a statement that the author takes responsibility for the entire contents of the patch, including any parts that were generated or assisted by AI tools

evidence.quote: Current QEMU project policy is to DECLINE any contributions which are believed to include or derive from AI generated content.

the "Signed-off-by" label in a patch submission is a statement that the author takes responsibility for the entire contents of the patch, including any parts that were generated or assisted by AI tools or other tools.

domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly bans AI-generated or AI-derived content in contributions/patches, and assigns responsibility for the entire patch content (including AI-assisted parts) to the author via Signed-off-by. Both supervision level (banned) and accountability holder (contributor/author) are stated.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: The document covers patch/code contribution provenance and AI-generated content in patches only; it never discusses meeting recording, transcription, or notetaker bots.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule naming documentation, blogs, or design assets specifically
domains.reasoning: The policy language is framed around 'patches' and 'contributions' to code; it does not name documentation, blog posts, or design assets as a distinct category. Any coverage would come only from the ambiguous general term 'contributions', which the metric requires attributing to code_contributions only.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on AI use in moderation actions
domains.reasoning: The document states the project 'will decline any contribution' suspected of AI content, which is an enforcement action tied to the code_contributions ban, not a statement about AI being used to perform moderation actions such as triage, banning users, etc. No separate moderation-of-AI-use-in-moderation rule exists.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI-assisted review of patches
domains.reasoning: The document discusses human review tags (Reviewed-by, Acked-by) but never mentions AI being used to review contributions.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on autonomous/agentic use acting on the repository
domains.reasoning: The policy mentions 'code/content generation agents which are built on top of such tools' as examples of impacted tools within the code-generation ban, but this addresses generated content ending up in a patch, not an agent autonomously interacting with the repository (opening PRs, merging, etc.). No separate statement about autonomous agentic action exists, though the general restrictive stance toward AI tooling suggests a restrictive lean.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of energy, water, or carbon footprint
domains.reasoning: The document's rationale for banning AI content is entirely about legal/copyright risk under the DCO; it never raises energy, water use, or hardware/carbon footprint concerns.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of server load or hardware cost
domains.reasoning: No text in the document discusses infrastructure strain, server load, or hardware financing related to AI use.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on QEMU's own data being used to train models
domains.reasoning: The document discusses the copyright/license status of the material LLMs were trained on (a rationale for banning AI-generated content in patches), which concerns other people's work feeding AI models, not QEMU's own contributions, issues, or user data being used to train models. That distinct concept is never addressed.

unscoped_statements.quote: Current QEMU project policy is to DECLINE any contributions which are believed to include or derive from AI generated content.

The QEMU project thus requires that contributors refrain from using AI content generators on patches intended to be submitted to the project, and will decline any contribution if use of AI is either known or suspected.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: QEMU's policy is narrowly and clearly specified for one domain only: it bans AI-generated/AI-derived content in code patch submissions and assigns responsibility for such content to the submitting author via Signed-off-by, while explicitly carving out non-included AI uses (research, static analysis, debugging). It is entirely silent on notetaker bots, general content/documentation, moderation, AI-assisted review, autonomous agentic action, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and the project's own data being used for AI training.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
